pharm: Peripheral enkephalinergic/opioid receptor agonist; gastrointestinal motility regulator
quick: 100-200 mg three times daily before meals
summary: Trimebutine (commonly as trimebutine maleate) is a gastrointestinal motility regulator and antispasmodic used for irritable bowel syndrome and other functional gastrointestinal disorders, including abdominal pain, bloating, and altered bowel habit, and to manage postoperative paralytic ileus. It acts peripherally on enkephalinergic (opioid) receptors of the gut to normalize abnormal motility - stimulating hypomotile and relaxing hypermotile bowel. It is not approved by the US FDA; this record is based on EU/SmPC and BNF-type references. It is generally well tolerated.
indications: Symptomatic treatment of irritable bowel syndrome (abdominal pain, bloating, altered bowel habit)
Symptomatic relief of functional gastrointestinal motility disorders
Management of postoperative paralytic ileus (in some regions)

dosage.c: Irritable bowel syndrome / functional GI disorders (adults)
dosage.n: Often taken before meals; adjust to response
Parenteral formulations available in some countries

dosage.d: Weight-based dosing per local product labeling
dosage.n: Use only per pediatric labeling where available

admin: Use the suspension formulation for children where available, dosed by weight
Reassess the need for continued treatment based on symptom response
Use the lowest effective dose for functional symptoms
moa: Trimebutine acts on peripheral enkephalinergic (opioid mu, kappa, delta) receptors of the gastrointestinal tract to regulate gut motility. It exerts a dual, normalizing effect - stimulating motility in a hypoactive gut and reducing it in a hyperactive gut - and modulates visceral sensitivity, thereby relieving spasm and abnormal transit without significant central opioid effects.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to trimebutine or formulation components
relative: Children below the age specified in local labeling
monitor: Symptom response and need for continued therapy

preg: There are limited data on use in pregnancy. As a precaution, avoid use during pregnancy unless considered necessary by the prescriber and the potential benefit outweighs the risk.
lact: There are limited data on excretion in breast milk. Avoid use during breastfeeding unless considered necessary.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is established; use standard dosing with clinical judgment.
hepatic: Limited data in hepatic impairment; use with caution as the drug is metabolized hepatically.

moderate: Other antispasmodics or motility-altering agents - additive or opposing GI effects
minor: Tubocurarine - trimebutine may reduce the duration of action of some neuromuscular agents (reported)
interactions.food: May be taken before meals; food does not markedly affect use.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction reported; general moderation advised.
interactions.diagnostics: No significant laboratory test interference reported.

emergency: Severe allergic reaction with swelling or breathing difficulty

monitoring: Symptom improvement and continued need for treatment
counsel: Take this medicine as directed, usually before meals
It helps regulate gut movement and ease cramping and bloating
Tell your doctor if symptoms persist, worsen, or new symptoms appear
Report any rash, swelling, or trouble breathing immediately
If you feel drowsy or dizzy, be cautious driving or operating machinery
Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding
pk: Symptom relief over days of regular dosing
Peak plasma concentration about 1 to 2 hours after oral dosing
Store per product labeling at room temperature, protected from moisture
pearls: Not FDA-approved; widely used in Europe, India, and other regions for IBS and functional GI symptoms - this record reflects SmPC/BNF-type official labeling
Unique dual motility action - stimulates a sluggish gut and calms a spastic gut via peripheral opioid receptors
Generally well tolerated with mainly mild GI and anticholinergic-type effects
Limited high-quality evidence; used for symptomatic relief in functional disorders
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not take a double dose.
overdose: Experience with overdose is limited. Expected effects relate to gastrointestinal and mild central nervous system symptoms (drowsiness, dizziness). Management is supportive and symptomatic; there is no specific antidote. Contact a poison control center for guidance.
